llm_observations.observation: The A3 threshold requires sites to be ≥10.0 km from small airports/airstrips. [FACT] The Eren-1 site is located in Kırklareli Province, northwestern Turkey, in the European part of Turkey (Thrace region). [INFERENCE] This region has mixed agricultural and forested terrain with several known small airports in the broader area. [ESTIMATE] Based on regional knowledge, there are likely small airfields within 15-20 km of the site coordinates, including potential agricultural airstrips serving the farming areas of Thrace. [INFERENCE] Given the agricultural character of Kırklareli Province and the systematic under-reporting of small airfields in Turkish databases, the estimated distance to the nearest small airport is likely 8-15 km, which places the site in a borderline zone relative to the 10.0 km threshold. Without comprehensive airfield survey data, the site triggers caution due to potential proximity violations.

The A2 criterion requires sites to be ≥7.5 km from Type 2 airports (military airfields with fast jets or heavy cargo operations). [FACT] The Eren-1 site is located in Kırklareli Province, northwestern Turkey, approximately 15-20 km from the Bulgarian border. [ESTIMATE] The nearest significant settlement appears to be Kırklareli city (approximately 15-20 km southeast), which would place most of its ~70,000 population outside the 5 km zone. However, without enrichment data on pop_density_5km or detailed knowledge of local villages within the 5 km radius, I cannot reliably estimate the aggregate population density. The cancelled status and rural location suggest density is likely well below 1,000/km², but insufficient data prevents a definitive assessment.
